craft_notes: Sthāyin same; color: drowned-yet-held (sustaining memory begins — NOTE: voice closes not in despair). Firing: turn kept whole (drown/hold in one breath); alone carries eva (exclusivity: nothing else holds); afloat keeps the water (ocean sustained as image, not swapped for safety). REJECTED OPTIONS (with killers): (a) afloat->safe -> killed: safe drains the ocean. (b) your virtue->thy worth -> killed: virtue (guNa) is exact. (c) heightening (only remembrance!) -> killed: plain statement holds more. Read aloud: DROWNED in SORR-ow-O-cean's WA-ter … re-MEMB-rance OF-your-VIR-tue a-LONE KEEPS-her a-FLOAT. Abhinavagupta frame: śṛṅgāra performed, not described — separated voice + landscape-answer are vibhāva; the cloud never told to carry a message is dhvani (suggestion doing the work); close in sustaining memory, not despair.

lines: remembrance of your virtue alone keeps her afloat.

reads_against.argmap: What protects the fallen? → Memory sustains, not despair.
c1_essence: Śṛṅgāra is performed, not described: the separated beloved's voice, her appeal to the cloud, and the landscape's answering her are all determinants (vibhāva) of the rasa. The cloud is never told to carry a message — that is dhvani, and it is what makes it the genre's first instance. The voice closes not in despair but in sustaining memory: the sthāyibhāva (love) transforms the sorrow (vyabhicāri) into something relishable. Kāma arises in the heart to kill; the beloved who is absent arises with him; the cātaka, thirsty for rain alone, begs water; the peacock-flock sounds at the clouds; she is protected only by remembrance of his virtue.
